self|grant_topic: The user is writing a grants aim page on molecular subtypes and endometrial cancer
assistant|grant_aim: Grant aim: identify and characterize molecular subtypes of endometrial cancer and investigate their clinical and biological significance
assistant|grant_objective_1: Objective 1: identify molecular subtypes of endometrial cancer using combined genomic and transcriptomic approaches
assistant|grant_objective_2: Objective 2: investigate clinical and biological significance of the molecular subtypes, including association with patient outcomes and therapy response
assistant|grant_objective_3: Objective 3: develop biomarkers for early detection and prognosis of endometrial cancer based on the identified molecular subtypes
assistant|grant_methods: Methods: comprehensive genomic and transcriptomic analysis of endometrial cancer samples via next-generation sequencing, plus unsupervised and supervised machine learning, with validation in an independent cohort
assistant|grant_expected_outcomes: Expected outcomes: identification of novel molecular subtypes of endometrial cancer and development of biomarkers for early detection and prognosis, leading to improved patient outcomes
assistant|grant_impact: Impact: the proposed research would provide new insights into molecular mechanisms of endometrial cancer and pave the way for new diagnostic and therapeutic strategies
assistant|endometrial_cancer_epidemiolog: Endometrial cancer is the most common gynecological malignancy in developed countries, and its incidence is increasing worldwide
assistant|endometrial_cancer_survival: Despite advances in surgical and radiation therapy, the survival rate for advanced stages of endometrial cancer remains poor
assistant|grant_motivation: Understanding the molecular mechanisms underlying development and progression of endometrial cancer is crucial to improve diagnosis and treatment
assistant|grant_validation_approach: Validation and significance investigation will use a combination of functional and bioinformatic approaches on an independent cohort
